    ## Day 1. Cairns to Daintree Rainforest
    ## Your adventure begins with an afternoon pick-up in a [luxury 4WD](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-categories/vehicle) from your Cairns accommodation. Embark on an unforgettable journey from Cairns to the charming Port Douglas and the captivating Cape Tribulation, experiencing the beauty of Australia's tropical paradise through scenic landscapes and thrilling adventures. Take in panoramic views of the Daintree Rainforest, Coral Sea, and Great Barrier Reef from Alexandra Lookout. Check in at the eco-friendly Ferntree Rainforest Lodge and unwind amidst the soothing sounds of the jungle. As the sun sets, stroll along the idyllic Myall Beach for a serene experience. For the ultimate rainforest adventure, join the optional famous Daintree Rainforest Night Walk. Led by expert guides, unveil the hidden secrets of nocturnal creatures in this ancient world. This condensed yet action-packed itinerary will leave you with cherished memories of the unparalleled beauty of Port Douglas to Cape Tribulation. ‍Accommodation: [Ferntree Rainforest Lodge](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/agent-code-pages/ferntree-rainforest-lodge) ‍Meals: Welcome Dinner at [Cassowary Restaurant](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/agent-code-pages/ferntree-rainforest-lodge)
    ## Day 2. Daintree Rainforest
    ## Flop and drop by the stunning lodge pool, or explore where the Great Barrier Reef meets the Daintree Rainforest. In the morning embark on a half-day adventure with your local guides. Discover wildlife on boardwalks, satisfy your sweet tooth at the Daintree Ice Cream Factory and gain insights into the recent cyclones impact on the area. Enjoy a sumptuous lunch at the Cassowary Restaurant, a hidden gem nestled within the vibrant rainforest. The afternoon offers you the freedom to explore or partake in various tours available in town. Some tours might need to be booked in advance. ‍Accommodation: [Ferntree Rainforest Lodge](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/agent-code-pages/ferntree-rainforest-lodge) ‍Meals: Breakfast, lunch and dinner at [Cassowary Restaurant](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/agent-code-pages/ferntree-rainforest-lodge)
    ## Day 3. Daintree Rainforest to Wolverton Station
    ## Begin your day with an exhilarating journey along the famous 4WD [Bloomfield Track](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/bloomfield-track), heading north to the historic Cooktown. Weather permitting, embrace the thrill of river crossings en route to your destination. The day's highlight awaits at the spectacular [Wujal Wujal Falls](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/bloomfield-falls), where you'll be treated to a interpretive walk, by Far North Escapes. Along the way, we'll stop at the iconic [Lions Den Hotel](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/lions-dens-hotel). Established in 1875, its walls are adorned with signatures from around the world—a tradition harking back to the old mining days. Immerse yourself in the hotel's lively atmosphere, often featuring live entertainment. Upon reaching [Cooktown](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/category/cooktown), soak in stunning views before venturing along the Peninsula Developmental Road to Wolverton Station "[Wildwishes](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/wild-wishes-at-wolverton-station)" in the Archer River Region. Here, experience a taste of authentic station life—it's the only station in Far North Queensland with historic cattle droving routes from the 1900s. Settle in for a cozy billy tea and captivating storytelling. Indulge in a truly unique experience as you spend the night at the exclusive[ Wildwishes Glamping Tent](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/wild-wishes-at-wolverton-station), situated at Wolverton Station, Archer River. This is the ultimate glamping destination in [Cape York](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-categories/cape-york). ‍Accommodation: [Wildwishes Glamping Tent](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/wild-wishes-at-wolverton-station) (FNE Exclusive use). Located at [Wolverton Station](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/wild-wishes-at-wolverton-station), Archer River. ‍Meals: Breakfast at [Cassowary Restaurant](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/agent-code-pages/ferntree-rainforest-lodge), Lunch and Dinner catered by Far North Escapes.
    ## Day 4. Wolverton Station to Iron Range National Park
    ## Over the next two days we travel back toward the coastline, experiencing the Lockhart River region. Visiting untouched waterfalls, and the long coastline of stunning[ Chilli Beach](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/iron-range-national-park). We also stop to explore the Lockhart River Art Centre which continues to encourage, work with, promote and represent local artist and their diverse range of artworks through paintings, ceramics, basket weaving and prints. A highlight will be experiencing the [Iron Range National Park](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/iron-range-national-park) with long sweeping beaches, rocky out crops, and the largest area of low land tropical Rainforest in Australia. Our afternoon arrival brings us to [The Temple Cape York](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/the-temple-cape-york): off-grid, isolated living at its finest. This is a great location with something for everyone! Fishing addicts, bike enthusiasts, bird watchers, military history buffs, and general lovers of life who want to just soak in the sea views. ‍Accommodation: [The Temple Cape York](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/the-temple-cape-york) (FNE Exclusive use). Located in Lockhart, just 10 mins from iconic [Chilli Beach](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/iron-range-national-park). ‍Meals: Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner catered by Far North Escapes.
    ## Day 5. Choose to relax, undertake activities, or explore Iron Range National Park
    ## Sleep in, or rise early with a sunrise coffee on the deck overlooking Chilli Beach and the Great Barrier Reef — either way, you’re starting the day right. Today is all about slowing down and soaking it all in. Your guides will take you exploring through the stunning Iron Range National Park, with its rich rainforest and chances to spot unique wildlife. Back at The Temple, cool off in the brand new pool, wander the shoreline with sand under your feet, or just let the rhythm of the waves set your pace. It’s the ultimate blend of chill and adventure, all in one serene, off-grid hideaway. In the past, we’d often visit Maʼalpiku — “Restoration Island” — to spend time with the inspiring David Glasheen. Sadly, Resto Dave passed away this year. It was a true privilege to know him, and we miss him dearly.
    ## Day 6. Iron Range National Park to Bramwell Station
    ## Today we travel wind inland to [Bramwell Station](https://www.farnorthescapes.com.au/blog-posts/bramwell-station), the most northerly cattle station in Australia. We are treated toa Station Talk followed by live entertainment.     ## HANDCRAFTED GNOCCHIItalian Cook & Dine Experience
    ## Winter Warmers Edition
    Cold outside.
    Inside? **Golden arancini. Pillowy gnocchi. Lemon ricotta. Pistachio pesto. Crisp cannoli.**
    This is winter, but with Italian sunshine on the table.
    **Handcrafted Gnocchi** is Roving Larder’s Italian Cook & Dine experience — hands-on, generous, bright, comforting, and absolutely worth leaving the couch for.
    You’ll cook.
    You’ll sip.
    You’ll learn.
    Then you’ll sit down at our long table and enjoy a beautiful Italian-inspired meal you helped create.
    It’s part cooking class, part dinner party, part little escape to Italy.
    No passport required.
    Just closed shoes and an appetite.
    **WHY YOU’LL LOVE IT**
    This is not just a gnocchi class.
    It’s a full Italian night out — with you in the kitchen.
    You’ll learn how to make soft, pillowy gnocchi from scratch, create flavour-packed sauces, fry golden arancini, and finish with crisp cannoli filled with lemon curd and mascarpone.
    It’s relaxed, hands-on, social, and deliciously satisfying.
    Perfect for date nights, birthdays, gifts, catch-ups with friends, team celebrations, or anyone who believes winter should come with arancini, gnocchi, cannoli, and wine.
    **HANDS-ON COOKING & DINING EXPERIENCE**
    This is not a cooking demo where you sit quietly while the chef does all the fun bits.
    At Roving Larder, you get involved.
    Your chef will guide you step by step through the menu, sharing practical techniques, timing tips, and little kitchen tricks that make Italian cooking feel achievable at home.
    You’ll roll gnocchi, shape arancini, build beautiful sauces, fill cannoli, taste as you go, and enjoy the buzz of a warm kitchen.
    Then comes the best part.
    You sit down at the long table and enjoy the meal you helped create — with good company, a drink in hand, and that very smug little feeling of, “Yes, I made this.”
    **WHAT YOU’LL COOK**
    ## Starter
    **Arancini with Bocconcini & Tomato Sauce**
    Crispy risotto balls with melted bocconcini centres, fried until golden and served with a bright, tangy tomato sauce.
    ## Main
    **Handcrafted Gnocchi with Lemon Ricotta & Pistachio Pesto**
    Delicate homemade gnocchi tossed with zesty lemon ricotta and finished with vibrant, nutty pistachio pesto.
    ## Dessert
    **Cannoli with Lemon Curd & Mascarpone**
    Golden, crisp cannoli shells filled with tangy lemon curd and mascarpone, topped with white chocolate and pistachios.
    **TECHNIQUES YOU’LL LEARN**
    During this Italian Cook & Dine experience, you’ll learn how to:
    - Make gnocchi dough from scratch
    - Roll and shape light, pillowy gnocchi
    - Create a vibrant lemon ricotta and pistachio pesto finish
    - Prepare golden arancini with bocconcini centres
    - Fry safely and confidently
    - Fill cannoli with lemon curd and mascarpone
    - Add simple finishing touches with white chocolate and pistachio
    - Plate your dishes beautifully without overcomplicating them
    **WHAT’S INCLUDED**
    Your experience includes:
    - Chef-led, hands-on cooking
    - All ingredients and equipment
    - Apron use during the class
    - Welcome nibbles
    - Welcome drink
    - A generous Italian-inspired meal
    - Curated beverages with the meal
    - Recipes to recreate the dishes at home
    - Long-table dining in a relaxed, welcoming setting
    **ITINERARY**
    Please arrive **15 minutes before the class start time** so we can welcome you properly.
    We’ll begin with nibbles and a welcome drink while everyone settles in.
    Your chef will then introduce the menu, explain the flow of the class, and guide the group through the cooking experience.
    You’ll cook, taste, ask questions, learn new techniques, and enjoy the rhythm of a warm, buzzing kitchen.
    Once everything is ready, we gather at the long table to share the meal together.
    Good food.
    Good drinks.
    Good people.
    A very good winter night.
    **WHO IT’S PERFECT FOR**
    This experience is perfect for:
    - Gnocchi lovers
    - Italian food lovers
    - Couples looking for a cosy winter date night
    - Friends who want something better than another restaurant booking
    - Birthday celebrations
    - Gift experiences
    - Team outings and small groups
    - Anyone who thinks homemade gnocchi and cannoli sound like a very sensible life decision
    **PLEASE NOTE**
    Menus may vary slightly depending on seasonal produce and ingredient availability.
    Please wear **closed shoes** for safety in the kitchen.
    **If you have dietary requirements, please let us know at the time of booking so we can do our best to accommodate you.**
    **BOOK YOUR ITALIAN WINTER ESCAPE**
    Don’t just sit through winter.
    Make it delicious.
    Join us for **Handcrafted Gnocchi** — a warm, hands-on Italian Cook & Dine experience.

    Set on the beautiful **Collie River at Minningup Pool**, this **2-hour guided kayaking session** takes place on calm, sheltered waters—perfect for first-time paddlers, confident kids and families looking for a safe, enjoyable and meaningful outdoor activity in Collie.
    **What to Expect**
    ## Fun, Safe and Easy Kayaking
    Your session begins with a friendly safety briefing and simple paddling instruction to help everyone feel confident on the water. The group stays together and moves at a relaxed family pace while exploring the natural surroundings of Minningup Pool.
    ## Family-Friendly Paddling
    This experience is designed specifically for families. There’s no pressure and no rushing—just gentle paddling, floating, exploring and sharing moments together.
    ## Swim, Splash and Play
    Depending on conditions, children and adults can enjoy supervised opportunities for a dip, splash or cool-off during the session.
    ## Nature Discovery
    Learn about local wildlife, listen to the sounds of the river and help kids build a deeper appreciation for nature, mindful moments and adventure.
    **Choose Your Session**

    Our Private 10 day tour travels across the most impressive & unforgettable locations of Australia. For the entire duration of the tour, from greeting you on arrival at Sydney airport, to bidding you farewell in Melbourne, you will be accompanied by one of our guides fluent in your language. You won't need to worry about a thing on this immersive luxury experience of Australia we travel in the utmost comfort & style with Australia's best guides taking care of your every need!
    Relax and be enchanted by the beaches & clear blue waters of Sydney harbour, the red sands of Uluru & the scenery of the stunning Great Ocean Road. Enjoy & be enthralled by bustling streets, dinners looking out over big city lights & the vast empty expanses of the red centre where you'll dine whilst gazing upon the Milky Way & it's billion bright stars.
    Rest assured you'll be exhilarated by the best of luxury Australia that you encounter on this unforgettable 10 day experience of life as it should be. This experience is ideal for families, groups of friends & couples looking for a honeymoon experience of Australia. No matter whether you are booking for a group of 12 adults, or 1 Adult traveling with 3 children (or any other combination of people) we will tailor the whole experience to be perfect for you!
    NOTE: Groups of 12 people maximum .
    Bookings within 60 days of arrival will be subject to price on application.
    **ITINERARY**
    DAY 1 **ARRIVAL- SYDNEY WALKING TOUR & OPERA HOUSE TOUR**
    Lunch & Dinner
    You will either be met in the morning at the airport by your guide and transferred to your hotel in a private vehicle, or for those already in sensational Sydney, you will meet your guide & group at the hotel lobby for your Welcome lunch. After we take a short walking tour of the City before enjoying a Private Tour of the Sydney Opera House. Dinner and welcome drinks will be in the hotel restaurant tonight.
    DAY 2 **SYDNEY CITY & BEACHES TOUR **
    Breakfast, Lunch
    Sydney is full of incredibly beautiful ‘must see’ sights and landmarks that are scattered across this immense harbour city. On this tour you will see them all. Nestled below the Sydney Harbour Bridge, the area known as ‘The Rocks’ is the birthplace of European settlement in Australia. We visit the stunning Royal Botanic gardens with the superb views of the Opera House and Harbour Bridge, pass by the Naval base of Wooloomooloo and the party area of Kings Cross before delving into further into the exclusive Eastern Suburbs (home to the cities rich and famous) & reaching the South Head at Watson's Bay.
    Onto Bondi, without a doubt Sydney’s and Australia’s most famous beach. Bondi is a lively neighbourhood centred around the famous beach. Enjoy some free time to grab a coffee or take a quick swim (sea water temperature raises up to 26 degrees Celsius in Febuary & March) or walk along the shore feeling the sand between your toes as the water rushes over your feet. Stopping for a walk & a photo at Darling harbour, we cross to the North side of the Harbour and go to see the beauty of Middle Harbour & the Northern Beaches. Elegant homes perched on hillsides over-look yachts moored out front. A little slice of paradise, home to picturesque lagoons and many of Sydney’s most beautiful & popular beaches, the area deserves a whole day unto itself to truly see it all. We will see Narrabeen, Collaroy, Dee Why & Freshwater (birthplace of Australian surfing), the ever popular Manly and enjoy a restaurant lunch. From the North Head at Manly we take in the remarkable view of the Harbour. See the cliffs of the South Head and the entrance from the Pacific Ocean known as the ‘Gap’ with the city skyline off in the distance. Tonight, dinner is at your leisure, maybe at one of the great places you've discovered today.
    DAY 3 **FREE MORNING & SYDNEY HARBOUR LUXURY BOAT CRUISE**
    Breakfast
    The day starts with a free morning. You have time for optional activities such as an incredible scenic flight or the Sydney Harbour Bridge Climb. At midday the group will meet in the hotel lobby for you departure to your private luxury boat cruise of Sydney Harbour. Lunch will be served onboard & there are ensuite bedrooms for anyone needing a siesta. Tonight, dinner is at your leisure.
    Optionals:
    - Sydney Harbour scenic flight
    - Sydney Harbour Bridgeclimb
    DAY 4 **BLUE MOUNTAINS**
    Full Board
    Only 90 minutes from Sydney, the scenery of the Blue Mountains is truly magnificent. See canyons, valleys, huge vertical sandstone cliffs and any number of beautiful waterfalls trickling slowly over ancient eroded escarpments. The Blue Mountains is an Australian tourist Mecca & with that in mind we keep one step ahead of the crowd. We take you away from the crowds in our small tour vehicles to see places other companies cannot access. We give you the very best private tour so you can truly appreciate the Blue Mountains in all their splendor. See some of Australia’s plethora of unique flora and fauna and to get an understanding of Australia outside of the Concrete Jungle.Tonight we have a private transfers to & from one of Sydney's premier restaurants.
    DAY 5 FLY SYDNEY – ULURU. **ULURU TOUR & SUNSET CANAPES**
    Full Board
    After a relaxed breakfast we take our flight to Uluru in the Red Centre, the very heart of Australia. We enjoy lunch at our hotel then take an afternoon tour of the majestic Uluru, the gigantic red monolith inside the world heritage Uluru Kata-Tjuta National Park. Finishing our day with canapes & a beverage as we watch the sunset on the ancient rock before returning to the hotel and enjoying a gourmet dinner at the Arnguli Grill & Restaurant.
    DAY 6 **KATA-TJUTA TOUR & FREE AFTERNOON**
    Breakfast & lunch
    This morning we go back into the park on our customised tour to get up close with the other equally stunning ancient formation inside the national park- Kata-Tjuta, the 36 enormous domes known to the Anangu people as 'the Many Heads' (Kata-Tjuta). We lunch together, then you have some free time to take the opportunity to relax by the pool, or take a helicopter flight, and maybe book a dinner on a sand dune under the billion stars of the Milky Way.
    Optionals:
    - Scenic Flights
    - Sounds of Silence dinner
    DAY 7 FLY ULURU - MELBOURNE. **EUREKA 8****9th FLOOR DINNER**
    Full Board
    Start the day with a relaxed breakfast before taking our flight to magnificent Melbourne, Australia's capital of culture & fashion. This afternoon you will have a few hours to relax before tonight's dinner in the acclaimed Eureka 89 restaurant up the top of the famous Sky Tower over looking Melbourne's city centre and the Yarra River.
    DAY 8 **MELBOURNE CITY TOUR & FREE AFTERNOON**
    Breakfast & Lunch
    This morning we take a half day tour of Melbourne before we lunching together at our hotel. Free afternoon to discover more of Melbourne & have dinner this evening at your leisure.
    Optional activity tonight: we can go together to see an AFL football game at the largest stadium in Australia seating over 100,000 people.
    DAY 9 **GREAT OCEAN ROAD SCENIC FLIGHT & FREE AFTERNOON**
    Full Board
    Today we take our private scenic flight in our chartered plane as we take in some of the most dramatic coastline anywhere on Earth. Known for very good reason as the Shipwreck Coast, among many fascinating spectacles to behold, today you’ll be witness to the magical 12 Apostles, towering rock stacks that rise up majestically out of the wild Southern Ocean. Upon return to the hotel we lunch together before a free afternoon & meeting tonight for our farewell dinner.
    DAY 10 **DEPARTURE FROM MELBOURNE**
    Breakfast
    After breakfast & 9 night's together it is sadly day number 10- departure day. We transfer to the airport and say our farewells.

    Bakery - Open 7 days, 7.00am to 4.00pm
    **The Piccadilly Valley **
    Skirted with vineyards, orchards market gardens and native bush. This area is renowned internationally as one of Australia’s most vibrant cool climate wine regions and stunning scenery.
    **CRFT Wines**
    Organic single-vineyard wines, CRaFTed in the Adelaide Hils by winemakers Candice Helbig and Frewin Ries. Small batch wine only, with a focus on Adelaide Hills Pinot Noir, Gruner, Veltliner and Chardonnay, and with Barossa Valley Mencia and Shiraz, all certified Organic with NASSA. CRFT choose practices that are good for the environment, animals and people. Relax at their Carey Gully Tasting Room and enjoy sweeping vineyard views.
    Cellar Door - Open Friday to Sunday, 12.00pm to 5.00pm
    [https://www.crftwines.com.au](https://www.crftwines.com.au/)
    **Tapanappa Australia**
    Tapanappa is the ongoing mission of celebrated winemaker Brian Croser and his family to make world-class wines from the most distinguished sites in South Australia. The winery and cellar door sit at the foot of the oldest vineyard in the Adelaide Hills – The Tiers Vineyard – which is globally recognised for its outstanding Chardonnay and hosts the wines of [DAOSA](https://terreaterre.com.au/daosa/) and [Terre à Terre](https://terreaterre.com.au/terre-a-terre/).
    Cellar Door - Open 7 days, 11.00am to 4.00pm
    [https://tapanappa.com.au](https://tapanappa.com.au/)
    **Greenhill Wines**
    Greenhill Wines is a vineyard, cellar door and café. The beautiful landscape is reflected in the wine, food and strong community. Grapes for our wines are all sourced within 2.5km of the winery, all hand-picked and fermented with selected or vineyard yeasts. Our high altitude cool climate vineyards allow harvest of balanced grapes minimising wine making interventions. Our sparkling wines are made using the traditional bottle fermented method.
    Cellar Door - Open Friday to Sunday & Public Holidays, 11.00am to 5.00pm
    [https://greenhillwines.com.au](https://greenhillwines.com.au/)
    **Casa Freschi**
    David Freschi is a quality-obsessed, innovative vigneron producing single-vineyard wines from Ashton, Adelaide Hills, and Langhorne Creek. All wines are grown in harmony with nature protected with organic fungicides. The vineyards are hand pruned, hand harvested and managed organically. Minimal tillage and handling, gravity racked and produced without fining, filtration or additives, except for a small addition of sulphur dioxide at bottling.
    Cellar Door - Open Friday to Sunday, 12.00pm to 5.00pm
    [https://casafreschi.com.au](https://casafreschi.com.au/)
    **Ashton Hills Vineyard**
    Ashton Hills was founded by Stephen George in 1982 and since that time it has built a reputation as one of Australia’s finest proponents of Pinot Noir and cool climate whites. With a focus on minimal intervention and movement they are able to capture the true expression of their unique site. Visit the rustic cellar door with its stunning views over the Piccadilly Valley and experience the range of award-winning wines.
    Cellar Door - Open Friday to Monday, 11.00am to 5.00pm
    [https://www.ashtonhills.com.au](https://www.ashtonhills.com.au/)
    **Cherry Bomb Café**
    Cherry Bomb Café is a rustic bakery set inside a converted 1870s stone house with an enormous wood-fired scotch oven used to bake sourdough bread, pies, pasties, sausage rolls and other traditional bakery fare. Warming soups, toasties, sweet nibbles, pies and cakes all made where possible with locally sourced produce, alongside coffee that’s roasted down the road. The rooms are cosy, eclectic and filled with flowers, books and velvet couches.
    Café - Open Wednesday to Sunday, 8.00am to 3.00pm
    [https://www.instagram.com/cherry_bomb_cafe_ashton/](https://www.instagram.com/cherry_bomb_cafe_ashton/)
    **Lofty Valley Estate **
    Keep an eye open for Lofty Valley Estate, set on 32 acres of natural bush in a steep valley. The boutique winery was sold in 2024 with their high-quality small-production of Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Rose, and Sparkling continuing to be available for purchase online.
    [https://www.loftyvalleyestate.com.au](https://www.loftyvalleyestate.com.au/)
    **Hills Collide**
    Whether you're just passing through for a quick glass, or want to stay a bit longer and make an afternoon of it, this recently opened cellar door is ready to welcome you inside. On the drinks menu, highlights include 2021 Blanc de Blanc, Methode Traditional, 36 months on lees; Solera-style vermouth made with Gewürztraminer, Muscat, and Riesling; and an Austrian-style harvest spritz made with Gruner, Veltliner, elderflower, and soda. Their kitchen prioritises high-quality, locally sourced produce from the Adelaide Hills and surrounding regions. The menu presents toasties with wild rabbit, goat, and venison, Danish-inspired open sandwiches, and Section 28 cheeses, including the raw milk, semi-hard Monte Chavel washed in pinot lees.
    Cellar Door - Open Saturday and Sunday, 11.00am till 6.00pm
    [https://hillscollide.com/](https://hillscollide.com/)
    **Wotton Family Wines, and in Summer months delicious Cherries**
    For over 150 years, over six generations, the Wotton family have worked productive, rolling farm land at Uraidla in the Adelaide Hill’s picturesque Piccadilly Valley. Their farm gate sales of 23 varieties of mouth- watering cherries that ripen over a 6-8 week period have been a favourite of the district. In 1994, the first wine grapes were planted in fertile soils previously used for fruit growing and market gardening. Since this time, the Wotton family have dedicated their focus on producing the highest quality cherries and wine grapes.
    Cellar Door - Open Friday to Sunday, 11.00am to 5.00pm
    Cherry Farm Gate Sales - Open During Cherry season
    [https://www.wottonfamilywines.com.au](https://www.wottonfamilywines.com.au/)
    [https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100064598683225](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100064598683225)
    **The Uraidla Hotel … the heart of the Community**
    After your e-Bike tour, a must is to drop in next door to the historic and award-winning [Uraidla Hotel](https://www.uraidlahotel.com.au/), a vibrant heart of the local community, committed to sustainability and eco-friendly practices with great food, local drinks and atmosphere in a welcoming community.
    Meals may be pre-booked in the restaurant or just walk in for a great pub meal.
    Wine tasting in ‘The Tank’ may be pre-booked with the sommelier to view one of the most extensive wine collections in the Adelaide Hills, featuring a curated selection of local Adelaide Hills wines, national treasures and international icons.
    [https://www.uraidlahotel.com.au/](https://www.uraidlahotel.com.au/)
    Open 7 days, 11.30am till late.
    **Important Information**
    · Riders must be at least 156cm tall
    · Riders to hold a valid drivers licence; photo ID may be required and photographed
    · Parent/Guardian participating may enquire if teenage children may also participate
    . Punctuality essential
    **Cancellation**
    · A full refund any time up to 48 hours prior to Tour start
    . Tours will be postponed or cancelled on extreme or catastrophic weather days
    **Dress Code**
    · Closed in footwear essential
    · Comfortable clothing for outdoor activity, suitable for the weather
    **What to bring**
    · Water
    · Sunscreen

    **Landscape and Long Exposure **
    **4 Days 3 nights Photography Weekend in Gerrigong/Berry**
    **Sun 17, 18, 19 20 Nov 2024**
    **FULL PRICE: $1860**
    **DEPOSIT: $440**
    **LANDSCAPE and NATURE PHOTOGRAPHY**
    **Immerse yourself in a weekend of learning, exploring and sharing creative energy in Landscape and Seascape photography in the beautiful surrounds of Gerringong, Berry and Kiama districts only 2 - 2.5hrs south of Sydney.**
    This weekend concentrates on gaining confidence by learning the art of composing, assessing light, and achieving well exposed and dynamic images. We will also we looking at developing a series work in one of these genres this weekend.
    Arts photographer Sharon Hickey and owner of The Aperture Club will reveal her insider tips and demonstrate ways of working mindfully in a variety of locations along with Landscape and Nature expert Sara Corlis.
    We explore the use of light in landscape and nature photography and learn important elements of composition and its relationship with form. We will also be spending time evaluating our work and learning new ideas and concepts from well known natural photographers.
    This is a unique opportunity to work with a professional photographers in an outdoor environment in an area inspired by many great artists and photographers.
    Berry is surrounded by breathtaking flora and fauna and is located 2.30 hrs south of Sydney.. From spectacular ocean beaches through to rainforests and waterways Berry has a wealth of beautiful locations for us to explore and capture.
    Arrive early if you wish and do nothing else but relax, meet wonderful people, indulge in great photography and explore this amazing landscape.
    We work in a small group 6 to 8. We will take 10 but will have 2 tutors available.
    Check out our Gallery of Photos made our last trip.
    **WORKSHOP FORMAT**
    **DATE**: 17,18, 19, 20 Nov ** 2024**
    **LOCATION**: Berry Area 2.5hrs south of Sydney
    **GROUP SIZE**: Minimum 4 - Maximum 8 participants.
    **WORKSHOP INVESTMENT**
    · Weekend for $1320 Tuition Only
    · Accomodation $540 Only $180per night Corporate Rate
    **TOTAL $1860**
    Secure your place with a deposit - $440. The Balance due 4 weeks before Workshop date.
    **ACCOMODATION**
    We stay at THE MERCURE HOTEL in Gerringong, which offers spacious and beautiful rooms. The hotel offers a lovely restaurant and bar area to relax and swimming and spa facilities to really unwind. The Mercure have given us a good rate and also a wonderful place to edit our work and for tutorials.
    We have secured a corporate rate and per room is $180 a night even for the Saturday night!- so we are being looked after! If you wish to spend any extra nights these will be accommodated at the corporate rate.
    I have put aside 10 rooms so once you have booked your trip with us please call and book your room which are held under **The Aperture Club**.
    The Mecure Hotel Info
    https://www.mercuregerringong.com.au/
    **WHAT THE WORKSHOP COVER**
    · Creative camera controls
    Long Exposure methods
    · Advanced creative composition
    · Understanding light
    · Working with filters
    · Creative idea development
    · Setting mood and creating atmosphere
    · Developing personal style
    Painting with Light
    **DAILY PROGRAM:** - Can change daily
    The program gives you the opportunity to shoot 3 sunrises and 3 sunsets and a night shoot.
    This is incorporated with some lectures, editing sessions and possible extra day time shoots.
    There is some time to explore the township go for a beach swim and also relax.
    This is an immersive few days of photography and the aim is to think and feel photography whilst developing your individual approach and ideas.
    Note schedule can be altered depending on everyone's needs etc. and is suitable for all levels of photographic skills.
    **WALKING AND WEATHER**
    This is a gentle trip, which requires a low level of fitness. There will be a small amount of walking to and from
    locations, occasionally on uneven surfaces with steps and inclines. If you have any doubts about your ability, please contact Sharon directly.
    When you book you will receive a detailed packing list to help you plan.
    **MEALS**
    Meals are not included in the tuition price but we will look at affordable and enjoyable options.
    There are plenty of cafes and restaurants around that suits all dietry needs and we can organise a picnic lunch if we so desire.
    Approx dinner costs excl drinks $25 - $35.
    BYO Alcohol to hotel or bar available.
    **TRANSPORT**
    **Car:** Make your own way directly to Berry. Car sharing might be an option.
    **Train:** We are happy to organise pick up and drop offs to local train station. It's a very pleasant train journey from Central station.
    Most of our clients prefer to have their own transport for this workshop, so that they can come and go from Berry depending on their time frame.
    We will try to condense our outings to a couple of vehicles only on our photography outings depending on numbers. Whilst there I can take 3 to 4 people in my car and the same in Sara's car.
    **WHAT TO BRING**
    · Camera equipment
    · Tripod
    · Laptop with latest Adobe Lightroom Classic software (recommended) or a
    tablet with image processing software (Snapseed or Lightroom)
    · Wet weather clothing? Check weather forecast
    · Wind jacket for early morning adventures
    · Sturdy footwear
    · Day pack/camera pack
    · Torch
    · Water bottle
    · Please make sure you have booked your accommodation prior to the workshop
    **TESTAMONIALS**
    I can highly recommend the Berry photography weekend away, lots of variety, one on one input, relaxed atmosphere, high quality accomodation and meals, learn at your own pace, suitable for all levels.
    Tracye Hughs
    We look forward to welcoming you on our photography workshop very soon.
    Sharon and The Aperture Club Team
    **Contacts:**
    Sharon: 0411 370577
    Email: info@theapertureclub.com.au

    8:00am or 1:30pm Pickup - 5 Hrs Total

    **1:30pm Pickup from City 5:30pm Departure for 6pm return**
    ## Tamborine Rainforest Skywalk
    ## Overview
    The Tamborine Rainforest Skywalk offers a unique and immersive experience, allowing visitors to explore the lush canopy of the rainforest from an elevated perspective. Situated in the Gold Coast Hinterland of Queensland, Australia, this eco-adventure attraction provides an opportunity to delve into the natural beauty and biodiversity of the Tamborine Mountain region.
    ## Experience
    The Skywalk comprises a 1.5-kilometre long path that combines forest floor trails, 300 meters of steel bridges through the upper canopy, and a cantilever bridge that soars 30 meters above the creek and rainforest below. This design ensures that visitors can appreciate the varying layers of the rainforest, from the towering trees to the intricate undergrowth.
    ## Highlights
    - **Cantilever Bridge**: One of the most exhilarating parts of the walk, offering breathtaking views over the rainforest and the Cedar Creek below.
    - **Interpretive Signage**: Along the way, interpretive signs provide fascinating insights into the flora and fauna, as well as the geological features of the area.
    - **Bird Watching**: The elevated pathways provide an excellent vantage point for bird watching, with species like the Paradise Riflebird and the Albert’s Lyrebird often spotted.
    ## Eco-Friendly Initiative
    The Skywalk is constructed with minimal environmental impact in mind. The materials used and the construction process were carefully chosen to protect the natural habitat, ensuring that the ecosystem remains undisturbed for future generations.
    ## Glow Worm Caves on Tamborine Mountain
    ## Overview
    The Glow Worm Caves, located on Tamborine Mountain, offer a magical subterranean experience that showcases the bioluminescent beauty of glow worms. These man-made caves are part of Cedar Creek Estate Vineyard and Winery and are designed to provide a controlled environment where glow worms can thrive and be observed up close.
    ## Experience
    Visitors are guided through the caves, where the darkness is punctuated by the mesmerising blue-green glow of thousands of tiny bioluminescent creatures. The guided tours are educational, providing detailed information about the glow worms’ life cycle, habitat, and the science behind their bioluminescence.
    ## Highlights
    - **Bioluminescent Display**: The primary attraction is the ethereal glow created by the Arachnocampa flava, a species of glow worm native to Queensland.
    - **Educational Tours**: Knowledgeable guides offer insights into the ecological importance of glow worms and the efforts being made to conserve their natural habitats.
    - **Interactive Learning**: The tour includes interactive displays and information panels that explain the biology of glow worms and the environmental conditions they require.
    ## Conservation Efforts
    The Glow Worm Caves are part of a broader conservation effort aimed at protecting these delicate creatures. By creating a controlled environment, the caves help alleviate the pressure on wild populations, which are often threatened by habitat destruction and human interference.
    ## Visiting Tips
    - **Plan Ahead**: Both attractions are popular, so booking in advance is recommended, especially during peak tourist seasons.
    - **Wear Comfortable Footwear**: The Skywalk involves a fair amount of walking, so comfortable shoes are a must.
    - **Respect Nature**: Both sites emphasise environmental conservation. Follow all guidelines to minimise your impact on the delicate ecosystems.
    - **Bring a Camera**: The Skywalk offers stunning photographic opportunities, though photography inside the Glow Worm Caves is restricted to protect the glow worms.
    ## Additional Activities: Waterfalls or Shopping on the Gallery Walk
    ## Waterfalls
    For those looking to extend their nature adventure, a short walk from the Bus Parking leads to a serene Waterfall. This picturesque waterfall is a favourite spot for both locals and visitors, offering a tranquil escape within the heart of the rainforest.
    ## Highlights:
    - **Natural Cascades**: The falls cascade into a series of natural rock pools, perfect for some fantastic Photos.
    - **Picnic Areas**: Several well-maintained picnic spots with tables and benches provide an ideal setting for a relaxing lunch surrounded by nature.
    - **Walking Trails**: A network of walking trails meanders through the surrounding bushland, offering varying levels of difficulty and a chance to spot local wildlife.
    ## Gallery Walk
    For a more leisurely experience, visitors can spend some time exploring the vibrant Gallery Walk on Tamborine Mountain. This bustling strip is home to an eclectic mix of shops, cafes, and art galleries, making it the perfect place to indulge in some retail therapy or simply enjoy the local culture.
    ## Highlights:
    - **Boutique Shops**: Discover unique treasures in the many boutique shops offering handmade crafts, jewellery, and local produce.
    - **Art Galleries**: Explore the creative side of Tamborine Mountain with visits to numerous art galleries showcasing works by local artists.
    - **Cafes and Restaurants**: Take a break and enjoy a coffee or a meal at one of the charming cafes or restaurants, many of which offer alfresco dining with views of the mountain.
    - **Specialty Stores**: From gourmet chocolates and cheeses to artisan wines and spirits, Gallery Walk offers a variety of specialty stores that cater to every taste.

    ## WITH LOVE FROM PARISFrench Cook & Dine Experience
    ## Winter Warmers Edition
    Cold outside.
    Inside? **Golden scallops. Butter sauce. Silky Paris mash. Chocolate fondant.**
    This is winter, but make it Paris.
    **With Love from Paris** is Roving Larder’s elegant French Cook & Dine experience — designed for people who want more than dinner out.
    You’ll cook.
    You’ll sip.
    You’ll learn.
    Then you’ll sit down and enjoy a beautiful French-inspired meal at our long table.
    It’s hands-on, generous, delicious, and just indulgent enough to feel like you’ve escaped to a little Parisian bistro for the evening.
    No passport required.
    Just closed shoes and an appetite.
    **WHY YOU’LL LOVE IT**
    This is the kind of winter night that gets you off the couch.
    You’ll learn how to cook scallops properly, make a rich butter sauce, create silky Paris-style mash, dress a salad the French way, and finish with a warm chocolate fondant that delivers the real prize: that glorious molten centre.
    It’s elegant, but not intimidating.
    French, but not fussy.
    Impressive, but actually achievable.
    Perfect for date nights, catch-ups with friends, birthday gifts, team celebrations, or anyone who thinks winter deserves better than takeaway and trackies**.**
    **HANDS-ON COOKING & DINING EXPERIENCE**
    This is not a cooking demo where you sit politely and watch someone else have all the fun.
    At Roving Larder, you get involved.
    Your chef will guide you step by step through the evening’s menu, sharing the techniques, timing, and little kitchen secrets that make French food feel less scary and much more delicious.
    You’ll cook together, taste as you go, ask questions, and build real skills you can use again at home.
    Then comes the best part.
    You sit down at the long table and enjoy the meal you’ve helped create — with good company, a drink in hand, and that very satisfying feeling of, “Yes, I made this.”
    **ITINERARY**
    Please arrive **15 minutes before the class start time** so we can welcome you in properly.
    We’ll start with nibbles and a welcome drink while everyone settles in.
    Your chef will then introduce the menu, explain the flow of the class, and guide the group through the cooking experience.
    You’ll prepare the dishes, learn the techniques, and enjoy the rhythm of a warm, buzzing kitchen.
    Once everything is ready, we gather around the table to share the meal together.
    Good food.
    Good wine.
    Good people.
    A very good winter night.
    **TECHNIQUES YOU’LL LEARN**
    During this French Cook & Dine experience, you’ll learn practical techniques including:
    - **How to cook scallops properly** Golden on the outside. Tender in the centre. No rubbery disasters.
    - **How to make a rich butter sauce** Glossy, balanced, and deeply French.
    - **How to create Paris-style mash** Silky, smooth, luxurious, and absolutely worth leaving the house for.
    - **How to dress a salad with French vinaigrette** Simple, sharp, elegant — the French do not drown lettuce, and neither will you.
    - **How to master chocolate fondant timing** Set on the outside, molten in the centre, dramatic in the best possible way.
    - **How to plate with bistro-style elegance** So your food looks as good as it tastes.
    **SAMPLE MENU**
    ## Main
    **Golden Scallops with Butter Sauce & Paris Mash**
    Perfectly seared scallops served with a rich butter sauce and silky Paris-style mash.
    Elegant, comforting, and very French.
    ## Side

    **‘Awaken in the Wild’**
    Litchfield National Park
    Mother nature is your host.
    **Tour Outline**
    ## DAY 1 – DARWIN TO LITCHFIELD NATIONAL PARK
    ## Meet Your Guide and Begin the Journey
    Start your day by heading to the front of your Darwin accommodation, where you’ll find your expert tour guide ready to whisk you away into the outback.
    ## Initial Exploration
    Arriving in Litchfield begin your immersion by tackling some of the more common locales and options. Included in this will be short hikes on pathways, swims in the clear creeks and waterfalls and general out and aboutedness ! As the sun slides left we make our way to our en-suite accommodation for the night where you can relax on the deck of your room whilst the onsite chef prepares a well deserved feast.
    Catering – Lunch & Dinner
    ## DAY 2 – Explore some more
    ## Early Start and Light Breakfast
    Begin your day by rising early with the birds, savouring a light breakfast before embarking on our next set of adventures in Litchfield National Park.
    ## Off-the-Beaten-Path Exploration: A Bush Walk to a Remote Waterfall
    Today’s highlight is a bush walk leading to a remote waterfall, exclusively accessible by foot. Secluded, quiet, and pristine, this experience offers an unparalleled connection with nature. As you traverse the path, delve into the knowledge of native foods and resources, gaining insights into the traditional methods that the indigenous owners utilized for survival and continue to employ today.
    ## Educational Insights: Traditional Survival Techniques Unveiled
    Enrich your understanding of the ingenious techniques employed by the traditional owners to thrive in their environment. Uncover the wealth of information about native foods and resources, enhancing your appreciation for the sustainable practices still prevalent today.
    ## Challenging Terrain: Hike Details
    Prepare for a challenging hike covering approximately 6-10 km, featuring sections of trackless walking and steep climbs. This journey promises both physical exertion and breathtaking views, providing a memorable and invigorating experience.
    ## Interactive Evening Experience
    As the ochre colours intensify and daylight fades, return to camp for evening snacks and a relaxing campfire experience. Tonight showcases Top End cooking at its finest. Immerse yourself in an essential part of our experience by trying to ignite a campfire using bush craft techniques. Seize the opportunity to hone your fire-starting skills using nothing but sticks—tap into your inner caveman!
    Catering – Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner
    ## DAY 3 – OFFROAD & OUT OF SITE
    Day 3 kicks off with a proper outback breakfast at Ridge Retreat before we point the wheels toward some of Litchfield’s lesser-known offroad tracks — seasonal access permitting. This is the Territory at its rawest. Expect corrugations, creek crossings, dust, mud and a few surprises along the way.
    Today is for the adventurous. We’ll head well beyond the busy tourist spots and into remote country where the crowds disappear and the landscape takes over. Depending on conditions, we’ll tackle short hikes into hidden pockets of the park, cool off with swims beneath escarpments and waterfalls, and explore places few visitors ever get to see.
    Lunch is a relaxed wilderness picnic surrounded by monsoon forest and stone country — no cafés, no bitumen, no rush. Just good food and wild places.
    As the afternoon winds down, we’ll make our way south to the iconic Adelaide River Hotel for a cold drink and a chance to swap stories from three unforgettable days in the Top End. Then it’s back to Darwin, dusty, tired and properly connected to the Territory.
    Catering – Breakfast, Lunch
    ## What's Included ?
    - Pick up & Drop Off at your hotel
    - Qualified local Australian guide
    - Comprehensive exploration of Litchfield Park
    - All camping equipment
    - Accommodation – camping with optional upgrade to CABINS
    - Catering – where indicated
    ## [tour Features](https://ethicaladventures.rezdy.com/139816/litchfield-wanderer)
    ## Hikes and activities away from the crowds Flexible program to suit your needs and wants Bush craft elements** Swims in clear waterfall fed streams and ponds Ample time for relaxation Hiking and off road driving En-suite accommodation
    ## You bring!
    ☐ Hat
    ☐ Camera
    ☐ Water bottle
    ☐ Comfortable walking shoes
    ☐ Sunglasses
    ☐ Sunscreen
    ☐ Swimwear & Towel

Wellington Jewish Heritage Tour
==============================================================================
  RETENTION  99.8%   FILL RATE   9.5% (2/21 fields)   FINDINGS 2

SUPPLIER TEXT (what the model was given)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Jewish families journeyed from across the world to build new lives in Aotearoa. This tour traces those stories alongside Wellington’s wider heritage, Polynesian migrations, early settlers, and the Jewish immigrants who helped shape the capital. Visit historic synagogues and neighbourhoods with a guide who shares these stories with warmth and personal connection.
    Hosted by Aaron, your guide, historian and award-winning cook, this is more than a sightseeing tour. As a local with deep roots in the community, Aaron will walk you through a living history from the earliest Jewish traders who arrived on New Zealand Company ships in 1840, to the families who fled persecution in Eastern Europe and found refuge in what was once called “The Great Jewish Hospital.”
    **YOUR ** **JEWISH HERITAGE EXPERIENCE ** **TOUR INCLUDES:**
    **Full-day tour (6 hours). Kosher lunch, entry fees and guided commentary included. Available Wednesday to Sunday.**
    **Sexton’s Cottage**
    Learn about the New Zealand Company and its earliest Jewish traders who flourished on these shores.
    Jews arrived on one of the first New Zealand Company ships to Wellington in 1840, including Solomon Levy, Benjamin Levy and Abraham Hort. Hort’s journey was noted in the Anglo-Jewish publication The Voice of Jacob, which promoted New Zealand as a suitable destination for Jewish colonists, praising its favourable “climate, soil and commercial possibilities.” Although the hope of mass Jewish immigration never came to fruition, a vibrant community took root.
    **Bolton Street Cemetery**
    The first Jewish cemetery in Wellington, established in 1843 as a designated section within the Bolton Street Cemetery. Following a request by Abraham Hort, a specific area was allocated for Jewish burials, separating it from the Anglican and public sections. Visit the burial sites of the first settlers, Lipman Levy and Solomon Levy.
    **Holocaust Centre — “My Origin Story”**
    Aaron shares his family’s own story of forced migration from the Lithuanian Duchy. Russian Jewish migration was historically driven by state-sponsored antisemitism, pogroms and mass expulsions — over two million Jews fled the Russian Empire between 1881 and 1920.
    Hear the remarkable story of Annie and Max Deckston, who arrived from Russia in 1900 and farmed in the Hutt Valley before making a fortune in Wellington. Childless themselves, they used their wealth to bring 20 children to New Zealand from orphanages in Bialystok, Poland, setting up a home in Berhampore that became an island of orthodox Jewish observance in the city. Learn why the Aron and Beder families journeyed from Belarus in the 1930s and were assisted by those earliest immigrants who had already called New Zealand home.
    **Jewish Community Centre and Heritage Buildings**
    Visit the Jewish community centre and historical buildings connected to Wellington’s Hebrew leadership. Your guide will share the stories of the families and individuals who built and sustained the community over nearly two centuries.
    **Kosher Lunch**
    Enjoy a main meal and a beverage at a pre-booked venue. Weekday tours visit Bond Street Deli (kosher), with Best Ugly Bagel or Ernesto’s (great vegetarian options) available as weekend alternatives.
    Sample menu: kosher hot dogs, sabich and kugel, gefilte fish and caviar, bagels and challah, matzo ball soup, salads and pickles, potato latkes, lox and a schmear, rugelach and babka.
    **Parliament Grounds and The Beehive**
    Visit Parliament House on Lambton Quay, home to the debating chamber, Speaker’s office, and committee rooms. Built between 1914 and 1922, it replaced an earlier building lost to fire in 1907. Next door stands The Beehive, the iconic Executive Wing whose distinctive shape is reminiscent of a traditional woven skep. A Category I heritage building, it has housed the offices of government ministers since 1979 — including the Prime Minister’s office on the famous 9th floor.
    **Mount Victoria Lookout**
    A prominent feature of the Wellington landscape, the summit offers spectacular panoramic 360-degree views of the city, the harbour, and the hills to the west. A perfect way to get your bearings and take in the full sweep of the capital.
    Your tour concludes after the heritage experience. Your guide will then drop you back at your designated hotel or at the cruise ship.
    **ADDITIONAL STOPS (GUIDE’S DISCRETION)**
    If time allows, your guide may also include one or more of the following stops.
    **The Painted Ladies**
    Wellington’s iconic, colourful 19th-century Victorian and Edwardian villas. Visit a famous, historic, family-owned example on the slopes of Mt Victoria and see the prominent row known as the “Seven Sisters” on Oriental Parade.
    **The Wellington Sign**
    Positioned on a hillside in Miramar, this landmark offers a picturesque backdrop for photos and panoramic views of the surrounding area.
    **The Roxy Cinema**
    Tour the beautifully restored Roxy Cinema and discover its art deco features and cinematic history. Hear anecdotes about the theatre’s transformation from its origins as a 1920s venue to its current status as a modern cultural landmark.
    **The Weta Cave**
    Step behind the scenes at the creative home of Weta in Wellington. Take an exclusive glimpse through the windows of the Weta Cave and learn about the making of movie effects — from armour to aliens, creatures to costumes, and makeup to miniatures.
    **Wellington Cable Car**
    The highlight of any visit to Wellington. In just five minutes, you’ll reach the top of the Botanic Garden where panoramic views of the city and harbour await. Visit the Cable Car Museum to see the original cars and winding machinery and explore the Space Place Observatory.
    **Wellington Botanic Garden**
    Just a short walk from the Cable Car, the Lady Norwood Rose Garden features 110 beds set out in a formal geometric design with colonnades on three sides and the Begonia House as a backdrop. The flowering season runs from November through to the end of April.
    **RAINY DAY OPTIONS**
    Wellington is famously unpredictable, so your guide has indoor alternatives ready if the weather turns.
    **Old Government Building**
    Commissioned in the early 1870s, this remarkable building was originally planned in concrete and timber, but cost led to a decision to build in timber alone. Designed in the Italianate, Neo-Renaissance style — usually the domain of stone — the building is crafted to mimic an Italian stone palace. It remains one of the largest wooden buildings in the Southern Hemisphere.
    **Old Saint Paul’s**
    Marvel at the gothic-revival grandeur of Old St Paul’s, renowned for its exquisite wooden interiors and vibrant stained-glass windows. Your guide will share captivating stories about the church’s construction and its enduring significance within Wellington’s cultural fabric.
    Please be mindful that fewer than 5,500 Jewish people remain in New Zealand today. This tour is a tribute to their enduring story.

    ## English
    All customers must be able to understand English, as they are required to demonstrate a clear and thorough understanding of the safety briefing and the operational instructions, including the practical operation of the Jet Ski.
    **Price:**
    Price per Jet Ski - up to two riders per ski
    ## What to Expect
    Other than an experience of a lifetime, you’ll see some of the most picturesque cityscapes Brisbane has to offer. Your guided ride traces the meandering Brisbane River from Breakfast Creek to South Bank and back, blending skyline views, heritage landmarks, and calm river reaches perfect for jet skiing. While on tour, keep an eye out for local wildlife such as cormorants, pelicans, rays, and—on lucky days—dolphins moving with the tide.
    ## Your Voyage
    Your Brisbane River adventure begins at Breakfast Creek (Newstead) with check-in and a practical safety and controls briefing. After a short familiarisation, you’ll head downstream, taking in:
    - **Brisbane Powerhouse** – A striking riverside arts venue, originally an industrial powerhouse; great photo op with New Farm Park adjacent.
    - **Story Bridge** – Glide beneath the city’s iconic steel cantilever bridge; throttle back for a moment to enjoy the view.
    - **The Pink Mansion** – A head-turning riverside residence that always gets a second look.
    - **The Star Casino** – Skim past the city reach with views of Brisbane’s entertainment precinct (river conditions permitting).
    - **Queensland Maritime Museum** – A nod to Australia’s maritime heritage along the South Brisbane reach.
    - **Wheel of Brisbane (Turnaround Point)** – Circle at South Bank’s riverside hub with sweeping skyline vistas before beginning the return run upstream.
    The route offers a unique, ever-changing perspective of Brisbane—leafy parklands, heritage facades, and modern architecture—before returning to Breakfast Creek with a grin you can’t shake.
    ## Cultural & Historical Notes
    The Brisbane River—known traditionally as Maiwar—has been a life source for local First Nations peoples for thousands of years. Today, it frames Brisbane’s identity: the Powerhouse reborn from industry to arts, the Story Bridge symbolising connection and resilience, and South Bank transformed after Expo ’88 into the city’s gathering place.
    ## Flexible Pace & Photo Stops
    Our tours cater to your preferences. If you’d like a leisurely cruise with multiple photo pauses, your guide will build them in at safe vantage points. If you prefer a more spirited ride (within conditions and group ability), we’ll set a tempo that matches the experience level of participants.
    ## Please Note
    Poseidon Jet Ski Tours perform a practical competency skill test prior to the commencement of all tours. Poseidon Jet Ski Tours reserve the right to cease or terminate a tour if the driver demonstrates a level of incompetence or behaves in a manner deemed to be a risk to themselves or other users.
    We also advise checking the weather before making a booking.
    **Brisbane Forecast:** https://wind.willyweather.com.au/qld/brisbane.html
    ## Medical Conditions & Fitness
    It is a requirement to inform Poseidon Jet Ski Tours before the tour commences if you have a pre-existing medical condition or any other considerations that may need to be taken into account and could impair or inhibit your ability to operate the equipment safely and effectively.
    All customers must demonstrate a minimum level of fitness; you must be able to tread water with a life jacket on in the event you are separated from the jet ski.
    ## What to Bring
    - Protective sunwear clothing
    - Towel
    - Driver’s licence or alternative photo ID (e.g., passport)
    - Sunscreen
    - Water bottle containing water
    - Hat suitable for jet skiing
    - Camera / waterproof phone with lanyard (bringing a non-waterproof device is at your own risk)
    - Optional: your own stinger suit or wetsuit (seasonal)
    ## What’s Included
    - Life jacket
    - Sunscreen (if you forget yours)
    - Safety briefing and practical jet ski demonstration
    - Bottled water (if you forget yours)
    - Experienced guide
    ## Lost Items
    Each jet ski has a forward storage locker and a glove-compartment style area with a smaller internal compartment suitable for a mobile phone or small valuables. Please only bring what you require. Poseidon Jet Ski Tours is not liable for lost or damaged items. If wearing sunglasses, use a safety strap.
    ## Weight Restrictions & Age Limits
    - **Maximum individual weight:** 130 kg
    - **Maximum combined (tandem) capacity:** 200 kg (inclusive of riders and any items)
    - **Minimum driver age:** 16 years (under 18 requires parent/guardian signature)
    - **Minimum passenger age:** 7 years (when riding tandem)
    These limits support the comfort and safety of all guests.
    ## Weather
    Poseidon Jet Ski Tours reserve the right to cancel, postpone, or reschedule a tour due to adverse or unfavourable weather or river conditions. Your safety is our highest priority.
    **Expectations with weather forecasting (guide only):**
    - **5–10 knots:** Smooth conditions, light chop
    - **10–15 knots:** Partially smooth with moderate chop
    - **15–20 knots:** Mixed conditions with increased chop
    Note: River traffic, tides, debris, maintenance closures, and special events may influence speed zones, brief pauses, or minor route variations on the day.
    ## Meeting Point & Check-In
    - **Departure:** Breakfast Creek, Newstead (exact pin and parking tips provided on confirmation)
    - **Check-In:** Please arrive **20 ** **minutes prior** for registration, safety briefing, and gear fitting
    - **Licensing:** No license required for this guided tour
    ## Safety First
    - Guided group formation with safe following distances
    - Speed moderated for conditions, zones, and rider ability
    - Clear hand signals and radio guidance (where applicable)
    - Mandatory life jackets at all times
    ## If Time Slots Are Unavailable
    ## **Please telephone to discuss tour options.** We’ll do our best to accommodate your schedule.

SUPPLIER TEXT (what the model was given)

    ## Explore the Outer Great Barrier Reef — Far Beyond the Crowds
    Step beyond the shoreline and into one of the most remote, pristine sections of the Great Barrier Reef. Remote Reef Realms is an outer reef expedition designed for travellers seeking authenticity, depth, and meaningful connection with the ocean — not crowded pontoons or rushed snorkel stops.
    Here, the reef reveals itself in its purest form. Colours are richer. Water is clearer. Sound fades into silence. This is the Great Barrier Reef as it was meant to be experienced. The outer reef is not just a destination — it is a shift in perspective.
    ## Why the Outer Great Barrier Reef Is Different
    Unlike inner reef locations closer to the mainland, the Outer Great Barrier Reef lies 50–100 kilometres offshore, rising from deep-ocean foundations. These reef systems form vast underwater plateaus and dramatic walls, shaped by powerful ocean currents that deliver exceptional water clarity and biodiversity.
    This distance creates something rare:
    - Healthier coral systems
    - Larger marine species
    - Fewer visitors
    - A sense of true exploration
    Out here, nature sets the pace.
    ## A More Immersive Reef Experience
    This experience is designed for guests who want more than a surface-level encounter. Outer reef journeys allow time to slow down, observe, and fully inhabit the underwater world.
    During your expedition, you may:
    - Snorkel across expansive coral gardens in crystal-clear water
    - Drift along vertical reef walls alive with soft corals and reef fish
    - Watch turtles glide effortlessly through shafts of sunlight
    - Float weightless in silence, surrounded by living reef systems
    It’s less about adrenaline — and more about awe.
    ## Iconic Outer Reef Locations
    Access depends on sea conditions, weather, and vessel capability, but these renowned reef zones represent the finest outer reef environments in the region:
    **Osprey Reef**
    A remote Coral Sea atoll known for dramatic drop-offs, exceptional visibility, and thriving marine life. Famous among experienced divers and photographers for its scale and intensity.
    **Ribbon Reefs (Reefs 3–10)**
    Stretching north of Cairns toward Lizard Island, these reefs offer protected lagoons, outer walls, and seasonal wildlife encounters — including dwarf minke whales between May and July.
    **Bougainville Reef System**
    Wild, exposed, and rarely visited. Known for pelagic species, powerful currents, and raw reef energy.
    **Agincourt Reefs**
    Located on the outer edge of the continental shelf, offering vibrant coral colour, high fish density, and a balance of shallow snorkelling zones and deeper reef structures.
    ## Best Time to Visit the Outer Reef
    **Dry Season (May – October)**
    The ideal window for outer reef travel:
    - Calmer seas
    - Lower humidity
    - Excellent underwater visibility
    - Comfortable conditions for longer water sessions
    **What to Bring for an Outer Reef Expedition**
    This is a remote ocean experience. Proper preparation ensures comfort and enjoyment. Recommended essentials:
    - Reef-safe sunscreen — protects coral ecosystems
    - Rash guard or wetsuit — sun protection and warmth
    - Dry bag — keeps personal items safe offshore
    - Waterproof camera — capture reef life responsibly
    - Snorkel or dive gear (optional) — equipment is provided, personal fit preferred
    - Seasickness tablets — offshore conditions can affect even confident travellers
    ## Who This Experience Is For
    - Nature lovers and ocean enthusiasts
    - Travellers seeking meaningful, uncrowded experiences
    - Snorkellers and certified divers wanting deeper access
    - Guests who value quality over quantity
    If you’re looking for a fast stop or party atmosphere, this is not the tour for you. If you’re seeking one of the most powerful reef experiences available — you’re in the right place.
    ## Book Your Outer Reef Experience
    Outer reef expeditions operate with carefully managed group sizes to protect this pristine environment and ensure a premium experience.
    Group Size & Capacity To ensure a premium experience, our group sizes are strictly managed. Each voyage is limited to a maximum of 30 guests.
    ## Minimum Guest Requirement & Private Options
    - Standard Bookings: A minimum of 10 guests is required for the tour to proceed. If this number is not reached, we will contact you to reschedule or provide a full refund.
    - Small Group & Private Bookings: For groups of fewer than 10 guests who wish to guarantee departure, private bookings are available for a fixed minimum fee (covering operational costs). Please contact our Booking Manager directly to arrange this.
    ## Weather & Sea Conditions Operations depend on safe sea conditions.
    In case of bad weather: If we must cancel due to weather, we will contact you immediately. You will be offered the option to reschedule or receive a full refund.
    Due to distance, sea conditions, and conservation-led operations, availability is limited. Early booking is strongly recommended to secure your place on this exceptional outer reef journey.
    Discover the Great Barrier Reef where it is wild, vast, and truly alive.

This experience is ideal for families, groups of friends & couples looking for a honeymoon experience of Australia.     DAY 1 ARRIVAL TO SYDNEY
    Lunch & Dinner
    You will be met in the morning at the airport by your guide and transferred to your hotel in a private vehicle. Your guide will then greet your group at the hotel lobby before your Welcome lunch. After we take a short walking tour of the City before enjoying a Private Tour of the Sydney Opera House. Dinner will be in the hotel restaurant with welcome drinks during an Orientation tour briefing.
    DAY 2 SYDNEY CITY TOUR- Full Day
    Breakfast, Lunch
    Sydney is full of incredibly beautiful ‘must see’ sights and landmarks that are scattered across this immense harbour city. On this tour you will see them all. Nestled below the Sydney Harbour Bridge, the area known as ‘The Rocks’ is the birthplace of European settlement in Australia. We visit the stunning Royal Botanic gardens with the superb views of the Opera House and Harbour Bridge, pass by the Naval base of Wooloomooloo and the party area of Kings Cross before delving into further into the exclusive Eastern Suburbs (home to the cities rich and famous) & reaching the South Head at Watson's Bay.
    Onto Bondi, without a doubt Sydney’s and Australia’s most famous beach. Bondi is a lively neighbourhood centred around the famous beach. Enjoy some free time to grab a coffee or take a quick swim (sea water temperature raises up to 26 degrees Celsius in February & March) or walk along the shore feeling the sand between your toes as the water rushes over your feet. Stopping for a walk & a photo at Darling harbour, we cross to the North side of the Harbour and go to see the beauty of Middle Harbour & the Northern Beaches. Elegant homes perched on hillsides over-look yachts moored out front. A little slice of paradise, home to picturesque lagoons and many of Sydney’s most beautiful & popular beaches, the area deserves a whole day unto itself to truly see it all. We will see Narrabeen, Collaroy, Dee Why & Freshwater (birthplace of Australian surfing), the ever popular Manly and enjoy a restaurant lunch. From the North Head at Manly we take in the remarkable view of the Harbour. See the cliffs of the South Head and the entrance from the Pacific Ocean known as the ‘Gap’ with the city skyline off in the distance. Tonight, dinner is at your leisure, maybe at one of the great places you've discovered today.
    DAY 3 LEISURE DAY. FREE MORNING & LUXURY BOAT CRUISE
    Breakfast, Lunch
    The day starts with a free morning. You have time for optional activities such as an incredible scenic flight or the Sydney Harbour Bridge Climb. At midday the group will meet in the hotel lobby for you departure to your private luxury boat cruise of Sydney Harbour. Lunch will be served onboard & there are ensuite bedrooms for anyone needing a siesta. Tonight, dinner is at your leisure.
    DAY 4 BLUE MOUNTAINS- Full Day
    Full Board
    Only 90 minutes from Sydney, the scenery of the Blue Mountains is truly magnificent. See canyons, valleys, huge vertical sandstone cliffs and any number of beautiful waterfalls trickling slowly over ancient eroded escarpments. The Blue Mountains is an Australian tourist Mecca & with that in mind we keep one step ahead of the crowd. We take you away from the crowds in our small tour vehicles to see places other companies cannot access. We give you the very best private tour so you can truly appreciate the Blue Mountains in all their splendor. See some of Australia’s plethora of unique flora and fauna and to get an understanding of Australia outside of the Concrete Jungle.Tonight we have a private transfers to & from one of Sydney's premier restaurants.
    DAY 5 FLY SYDNEY – ULURU. ULURU TOUR & SUNSET CANAPES
    Full Board
    After a relaxed breakfast we take our flight to Uluru in the Red Centre, the very heart of Australia. We enjoy lunch at our hotel then take an afternoon tour of the majestic Uluru, the gigantic red monolith inside the world heritage Uluru Kata-Tjuta National Park. Finishing our day with canapes & a beverage as we watch the sunset on the ancient rock before returning to the hotel and enjoying a gourmet dinner at the Arnguli Grill & Restaurant.
    DAY 6 KATA-TJUTA TOUR- Half Day - FREE AFTERNOON
    Breakfast, Lunch
    This morning we go back into the park on our customised tour to get up close with the other equally stunning ancient formation inside the national park- Kata-Tjuta, the 36 enormous domes known to the Anangu people as 'the Many Heads' (Kata-Tjuta). We lunch together, then you have some free time to take the opportunity to relax by the pool, or take a helicopter flight, and maybe book a dinner on a sand dune under the billion stars of the Milky Way.
    DAY 7 FLY ULURU - MELBOURNE. DINNER ON THE 89th FLOOR
    Full Board
    Start the day with a relaxed breakfast before taking our flight to magnificent Melbourne, Australia's capital of culture & fashion. This afternoon you will have a few hours to relax before tonight's dinner in the acclaimed Eureka 89 restaurant up the top of the famous Sky Tower over looking Melbourne's city centre and the Yarra River.
    DAY 8 MELBOURNE CITY TOUR- Half Day - FREE AFTERNOON
    Full Board
    Start the day with a half day tour of Melbourne before we return to the hotel for lunch. You have the rest of the day free to explore the wonders of Melbourne. Optional activity tonight: we can go together to see an AFL football game at the largest stadium in Australia seating over 100,000 people.
    DAY 9 FLY MELBOURNE via GREAT OCEAN ROAD - COONAWARRA - KANGAROO ISLAND
    Full Board
    Today is action packed! This morning your eyes will feast on some of the most dramatic coastline anywhere on Earth as we fly over the world famous Great Ocean Road. Be witness to the magical 12 Apostles, towering, magnificent rock stacks that rise up out of the Southern Ocean. Flying via the majestic Grampians, we land at our private winery for wine tasting and a gourmet lunch. Then it's on to Kangaroo Island for our dinner & stay the night.
    DAY 10 KANGAROO ISLAND TOUR- Full Day
    Full Board
    We take a full day tour of Kangaroo Island to enjoy this most incredible & spectacular display of nature. The 18 kilometres of ocean that separates Kangaroo Island from the mainland has protected it against introduced species like foxes and rabbits that have decimated native animal and plant populations across Australia. The island is therefore a time capsule of Australia as it once was, with native animals and plants in abundance and delicate ecosystems unchanged for thousands of years. You will be utterly enthralled by KI as locals call it.
    DAY 11 FLY KANGAROO ISLAND - ADELAIDE- Half Day Tour
    Full Board
    This morning we fly to amazing Adelaide, the home of Australia's best food and wine, which of course, we indulge in! After checking into our hotel we leave for our lunch in the McLaren Vale wine region, only 45 minutes south of Adelaide's city centre. After lunch we take a city tour taking in all the highlights of this beautiful laid back city. Tonight we dine in one of Adelaide's most celebrated restaurants featuring all local produce.
    DAY 12 DEPART ADELAIDE
    Breakfast
    Sadly this is our 12th & final day together. After a leisurely breakfast we transfer to the airport and say our farewells. Hopefully you will travel on with wonderful memories of an extraordinary experience of Australia!
    **INCLUSIONS:**
    - Services of an Experienced Australian Guide fluent in your language who’ll escort the group during the entire extent of the tour

    **AUTUMN COLOURS PHOTOGRAPHY WORKSHOP**
    **TOTAL INVESTMENT**: $2200 Includes tuition, accommodation, breakfasts, garden entrances and 1 x picnic lunch.
    Please pay a deposit of $450 to hold your place via our booking link below. Note: the balance is due 4 weeks before the workshop starts.
    Autumn is a brilliant time to experiment with creative photography techniques—use shallow depth of field to isolate a single leaf, or shoot through foreground foliage to create soft, dreamy layers. Try intentional camera movement (ICM) with slow shutter speeds to turn trees into painterly streaks of colour and atmosphere. For a more abstract result, get in close with macro-style framing and focus on texture, patterns, and the tiny details that make the season feel alive.
    Autumn naturally gives you ready-made drama — rich colour, strong texture, and moody light — so creative techniques instantly look more powerful and intentional. The season also has lots of movement (falling leaves, wind in branches) which makes slow shutter effects and abstract blur really effective. Basically… autumn does half the creative work for you.
    **LEARN HOW TO CAPTURE THE COLOURS OF AUTUMN.**
    The warm, golden light of autumn mornings and evenings adds a soft glow to landscapes, enhancing the rich hues of the season. Trees shedding their leaves often reveal striking textures and patterns, while fallen leaves create natural, colourful carpets that add depth and interest to compositions. It’s a time when nature’s artistry is on full display, inviting photographers to explore and experiment with their creative vision.
    Photographing autumn colours is a delightful experience because the season offers endless opportunities for storytelling. Whether capturing the contrast of fiery foliage against an overcast sky or focusing on the intricate details of a single dew-kissed leaf, autumn encourages a closer connection to nature. The dynamic range of colours and textures provides a perfect canvas for photographers to play with light, shadows, and perspective.     Lesson topics include composition, tone, line, colour theory, self-critique, studying master landscape photographers and technical camera and processing tips. Lesson topics are guided by the needs of the group.

    Blackheath is on a high plateau about 1000 metres above sea level. Temperatures are generally lower than Sydney. Spring days in the Blue Mountains regularly begin with a misty morning that burns off by mid-morning. This is caused by cold air sinking into the valleys overnight and rising as the day begins and can make for very atmospheric (but chilly!) morning shoots. During spring, temperatures generally rise through the day, with crisp cool evenings. Err on the safe side and come prepared for wind, rain and temperatures from 10˚C- 20˚C.

      AUTUMN COLOURS PHOTOGRAPHY WORKSHOP
      Please pay a deposit of $450 to hold your place via our booking link below. Note: the balance is due 4 weeks before the workshop starts.
      Autumn is a brilliant time to experiment with creative photography techniques—use shallow depth of field to isolate a single leaf, or shoot through foreground foliage to create soft, dreamy layers. Try intentional camera movement (ICM) with slow shutter speeds to turn trees into painterly streaks of colour and atmosphere. For a more abstract result, get in close with macro-style framing and focus on texture, patterns, and the tiny details that make the season feel alive.
      Autumn naturally gives you ready-made drama — rich colour, strong texture, and moody light — so creative techniques instantly look more powerful and intentional. The season also has lots of movement (falling leaves, wind in branches) which makes slow shutter effects and abstract blur really effective. Basically… autumn does half the creative work for you.
      LEARN HOW TO CAPTURE THE COLOURS OF AUTUMN.
      The warm, golden light of autumn mornings and evenings adds a soft glow to landscapes, enhancing the rich hues of the season. Trees shedding their leaves often reveal striking textures and patterns, while fallen leaves create natural, colourful carpets that add depth and interest to compositions. It’s a time when nature’s artistry is on full display, inviting photographers to explore and experiment with their creative vision.

    The Loch Ard.

      3.45pm – Depart from Yarra Valley to be back to Federation Square at between 4.45pm-5.15pm.
      We have chilled coolers and waters onboard. We share the music, so you can pitch in with the Spotify playlist if you love your music whilst driving.
